resources.string: Only apps on this device can open the proxy. Turned on, it also answers other devices on your network and asks them for a login.

Other devices on this network can open the proxy, with the login. Without one, anyone on the same Wi-Fi could open every folder shared in your tailnet, so authentication stays on while this is on. Turned off, it goes back to what you had chosen.
Other devices on this network can open the proxy, and no login is asked of them.
Listens on %1$s, an address set by hand. Select this to choose the local network or this device only.
Stays on while access from the local network is allowed.
The proxy listens on %1$s, an address set by hand.
Listen on every interface. A login will be required.
No login on the local network

This proxy was already set to answer the local network with no login, and it still does: anyone on the same Wi-Fi can open every folder shared in your tailnet. Requiring a login closes that. Apps and devices that use the proxy now will need the login, and it will stay required while access from the local network is on.

The address the proxy listens on. 127.0.0.1 is this device only and 0.0.0.0 is every interface: the switch above sets these. Any other address is used as typed, and the switch then shows it as custom.
Only apps on this device can open it. To reach it from another, turn on “Allow from the local network”.
This device is on no local network right now, so only its own apps can open the proxy. Connect it to Wi-Fi or a cable.
